apparatus: Initially occupied spinless fermion orbital, energy epsilon. Independent semi-infinite nearest-neighbor bath chain with hoppingJ=1 is grandcanonical at knownT and chemicalpotential0. Sudden endpoint contactV=g*multiplier, followed only by the stated quadratic unitary Hamiltonian. Thermodynamic bath limit precedes long-time Cesaro average of orbital occupation. No other bath or equilibration channel.
calibration: Multiplier1, positive orbital energies. Throughout the parameter interval there are no outside-band poles, and local initial occupation disperses; the exact coupled Gibbs spectral occupation equals the quench asymptote. Each tested calibration curve is strictly monotone in g.
complete_shortcut: Exact surface Green function, full continuum spectral density, both localized-pole energies and positive residues; assign Fermi populations to every exact mode. This is a valid coupled-Gibbs closure, not a missing mode or eigenvalue error.
oracle: Same exact continuum term. Bound mode initial occupation is its overlap with the specified initial product covariance; its dot contribution is Z_b²*[1+V²*integral rho_surface(E)f(E)/(E_b-E)² dE]. Cesaro averaging removes cross terms between distinct bound energies.
independent_reference: Construct finite-chain one-particle Hamiltonian, diagonalize tridiagonal matrix, project initial covariance1⊕f(Hbath) onto eigenvectors and take its diagonal ensemble. Bath sine-transform eigenbasis is independent of the surface Green function. Check N128,256,512,1024 and extrapolate finite-size1/N correction.

prototype_summary.note: An initial arbitrary15%minimum-margin assertion failed on the extra negative-epsilon example. Preserved that result; no model trial or task grading was involved. Proposed nonnegative orbital gate range contains the other examples and avoids this weaker case.

physical_checks: Finite-chain mode populations remain[0,1]; particle number and total energy equal the initial state at roundoff. Mean instantaneous quench work is0 because the initial contact expectation vanishes. All final spectral weights sum to1.
remaining_before_full_package: Need independent peer/source check and approval. A full package would extend bounds/noise/corner/finite-size checks and preserve all prototype results; empirical difficulty unknown.

archive_audit.comparison: Closest conceptual predecessor: full Gibbs versus a symmetry-protected spin sector. New candidate has emergent spatially localized one-particle modes above a tunable contact threshold; weak-contact calibration needs no detector conditioning. It is still an equilibration/reachability failure and that overlap must be disclosed.

Initial interacting Gibbs spin-bath correlations, followed by local pulses. New apparatus starts from an explicit decoupled product and has exact Gaussian unitary dynamics; error is assuming final equilibration of newly localized modes.

Classical adiabatic actions during isolated deformation. New quench has no adiabatic approximation or assumed single temperature after deformation; bath continuum equilibrates local scattering states while localized spectral modes preserve preparation.
Composing exact reduced channels resets spin-field correlations between segments. New candidate has one sudden quench and a time-averaged observable; no interval factorization.
Scattering residence measurement versus phase derivative. New source retains continuum spectral density and pole residues; measured occupation is determined by preparation of those modes.
Driven bath sidebands and calorimeter energy assignment. New Hamiltonian is time independent after one quench and has no Markov/secular rate model.
